text: Write a program that reads its own command-line arguments and reports on them. Fill in the three blanks.
explanation: Run it with no arguments and it prints count: 0 — verified. That is worth checking rather than assuming, because in C the equivalent array's first entry is the program's own name and the count is therefore at least 1. Java's `args` contains only what the user typed after the class name. An assumption carried over from another language is exactly the kind of thing that produces an off-by-one nobody can see.
